sections.heading: 4. Days 22-30: Close the Evidence File and Apply Day 30/60/90 Decisions
paragraphs: Day 22 reconciles every pilot time entry and missing supplier bill. Day 23 recalculates site contribution and prepares written price or scope corrections. Day 24 submits invoices through the customer's actual purchasing channel and verifies receipt rather than merely recording an email as sent. Day 25 tests payroll and absence coverage against the next four weeks of scheduled work. Day 26 obtains the buyer's written acceptance, complaint list, or renewal decision. Day 27 audits chemicals, training records, equipment condition, and access credentials. Day 28 inspects the route's longest travel segment and measures whether a second building can fit without overtime or service-window collisions. Day 29 closes the cash forecast, updates concentration, and reconciles earned revenue separately from deposits and unpaid invoices. Day 30 produces a one-page decision record showing actual results, missing evidence, corrective owners, and the next review date. If the first contract remains unsigned, attach buyer-confirmed next steps and completed walkthrough records instead of inventing delivery statistics. Complete at least three measured proposals by this review. A credible pipeline can justify continued testing within the cash ceiling, but it cannot justify hiring the entire four-person pod or advertising unused capacity as an operating achievement.

Apply decisions in order: a Kill condition overrides everything, any Fix condition blocks expansion, and Scale requires every applicable control to pass. Kill means stop the affected offer, account, or expansion commitment; terminate service through contractual procedures and preserve safe continuity where necessary. Fix means assign one owner, a measurable correction, and a fourteen-day deadline. A negative contribution account gets one correction attempt; if the next two full service weeks remain negative, use its exit provisions. Scale means one adjacent site at a time, not immediately jumping to the eleven-person scenario. The standard delivery threshold is at least thirty-percent direct contribution, ninety-five-percent first-pass acceptance, ninety-eight-percent completion reliability, and no more than ten-percent labor overrun. Require ten inspected customer visits across two service weeks for Day 30, twenty visits across four weeks for Day 60, and forty visits across eight weeks for Day 90. Missing samples mean Fix and continued observation, never an assumed pass. Pause the affected task immediately for an uncontrolled serious exposure, unpaid earned wages, or lost essential coverage. Resume only after the specific deficiency is resolved and documented; averages cannot offset those failures.

Review cash and concentration alongside service results. After Day 30, cap cumulative launch burn at the lesser of $18,000 or opening unrestricted cash minus the $9,000 minimum reserve, while retaining the larger six-week committed-labor reserve whenever required. At $15,000 opening cash, cumulative burn therefore remains capped at $6,000 unless collected operating receipts offset new spending; fresh borrowing does not improve measured burn. A forecast reserve breach inside fourteen days stops new commitments immediately. Through Day 60, require no undisputed invoice more than fifteen days past its contractual due date; at Day 90, also require receivable days of thirty-five or less. Calculate receivable days as ending trade receivables divided by trailing sixty-day earned credit revenue, multiplied by sixty; exclude deposits and calculate only with a positive revenue denominator. Track customer concentration by signed monthly recurring fees, not pipeline value. One pilot customer is acceptable during validation; discretionary equipment or permanent staffing expansion requires the largest customer at fifty percent or less by Day 60 and forty percent or less by Day 90. Maintain ten-percent field capacity reserve and inspect every added site's first three visits before releasing further route growth.

Day 30: first customer delivery and contribution
Stop unsafe tasks immediately; exit negative contribution after one correction and two further losing service weeks.
Fewer than ten inspected visits across two weeks, or any standard threshold miss, blocks additional starts.
Ten visits across two weeks meet thirty-percent contribution, ninety-five-percent acceptance, ninety-eight-percent completion, and ten-percent maximum overrun.
Day 30: payroll liquidity and committed capacity
Stop commitments when a fourteen-day forecast breaches the greater of $9,000 or six weeks of committed labor payments.
Unconfirmed relief capacity or unresolved payroll records requires supervisor correction before another site can start.
Verified reserve, reconciled payroll, trained relief, and ten-percent spare field capacity permit one adjacent site.
Day 60: procurement progress and offer viability
Retire the current offer if ten qualified walkthroughs and five measured proposals produce five explicit buyer rejections and no win.
Zero signed contracts with dated procurement steps means continued testing, not hiring or automatic abandonment.
Require two unrelated paying customers and a buyer-confirmed next opportunity before adding permanent route commitments.
Day 60: four-week service and cost evidence
Exit accounts still producing negative contribution after their documented correction window and contractual notice process.
Fewer than twenty inspected visits across four weeks, or any standard threshold miss, requires a dated correction.
Twenty visits across four weeks pass all standard delivery thresholds without unresolved critical safety or access failures.
Day 60: collections and customer concentration
Freeze growth when reserve coverage fails or cumulative launch burn reaches its permitted ceiling.
Invoices over fifteen days past due or customer concentration above fifty percent block discretionary expansion commitments.
Keep largest customer at fifty percent or less, protect reserves, and collect without material overdue undisputed invoices.
Day 90: eight-week delivery and staffing readiness
Stop the affected service when serious unresolved exposure or lost essential coverage prevents controlled delivery.
Fewer than forty inspected visits across eight weeks, or missing trained relief, prevents another permanent staffing commitment.
Forty visits across eight weeks pass standard thresholds with ten-percent spare field capacity and inspected new starts.
Day 90: actual operating profit and pricing
Retire offers repeatedly generating negative direct contribution after documented scope correction and an unsuccessful repricing attempt.
Positive contribution but trailing thirty-day net margin below eight percent requires overhead or pricing repair.
At least eight-percent actual net margin supports cautious growth; twelve-percent performance supports the Base margin objective.
Day 90: collections concentration and protected cash
Stop expansion on any forecast reserve breach; pursue contractual remedies for persistently unpaid service rather than extending exposure.
Receivable days above thirty-five, materially overdue invoices, or largest-customer share above forty percent requires correction.
Require receivable days at thirty-five or less, timely invoices, forty-percent maximum concentration, and full labor reserves.

action_checklist: Assign owners to the four plays and map thirty named buildings with decision makers, access windows, and renewal dates.
Approve a $6,000 first-month launch-burn ceiling and protect the greater of $9,000 or six weeks of committed labor payments.
Build three measured proposals using ISSA task references, observed paid minutes, explicit scope boundaries, and at least thirty-percent modeled direct contribution.
Mobilize only authorized work with verified coverage, properly classified labor, chemical controls, medical-site responsibilities, and invoice instructions.
Reconcile pilot time, inspection outcomes, direct costs, customer acceptance, and cash receipts without treating deposits as earned service revenue.
Record Day 30/60/90 Kill, Fix, or Scale decisions using sample requirements, labor variance, contribution, collections, concentration, and reserve coverage.
